findings.issue: Fifteen actual worker handles live inside the consuming outer caller future and are joined only after all preceding fallible caller operations. Caller error/deadline drops original raw handle and loses original pending or completed worker outcome; Drop detaches. A panic before join has the same owner loss, but no production leak or native lifetime claim is made.
findings.remedy: Immediate actual ConnectionPeer Drop guard in an actual typed owner slot outside the consuming ten-second caller deadline. Borrow joins and retain Ready results exactly once. Current paths have no later await after join, so original joined failure can flow directly into the outside caller Result; add a completed-result slot only when a new later await actually requires retention. Finite cleanup retains completed worker errors/foreign JoinError; abort only observed unfinished owners before collecting. Do not use unconditional ConnectionPeer::stop as the sole completed-cancellation collector.

findings.issue: Three named peer byte collectors lack aggregate byte ceilings. read_until_closed has a real local five-second time limit; H2/H3 body loops have no own deadline and raw workers can outlive consuming caller deadline. Shared read_head already has 32 KiB limit; H2 read_frame has a 24-bit individual frame length but no aggregate body ceiling.
findings.remedy: Bound retained trailing HTTP1 bytes before growth using the zero-body contract; bound H2/H3 accumulated upload bytes to actual seven-byte payload before extend/copy. Preserve FIN/END_STREAM and socket-close classifications. H2 frame payload is allocated by shared support before local accumulation guard; do not claim a new per-frame allocation bound or modify that shared parser without root scope.

findings.issue: Local aliases precede std/external groups; several fixture bodies conflate setup, head/field observations, quiet guard, response writes, body collection, final response, release and joined-result validation. This needs operation paragraphs, not a blank line after every call.

qualified_additional_boundary.issue: Five lifetime channel receive errors and five send failures are explicitly ignored without local rationale. They are not worker result ownership; caller failure can close sender, so an original receive error is presently accepted as successful release.
qualified_additional_boundary.remedy: Specify normal completion versus locally requested caller shutdown, keep the actual client/response until the original release point, observe failed normal release and always collect original worker cause. Treat deliberate sender closure on caller failure as a documented shutdown choice, not automatically an unexpected failure or substitute result. Preserve actual RecvError if that path is classified unexpected.
qualified_additional_boundary.claim_limit: A channel close may be deliberate lifetime release. This review confirms ignored outcomes and unclear error contract, not a measured new leak or unconditional wrong-success claim.
